interpretation: Motivates specialized intent signals before an LLM. HMEG combines five experts for classification rather than injecting one expert’s outputs into generation.
Evaluate HMEG instruction-manipulation signals with explicit trusted/untrusted context and report the limits of isolated-prompt classification.
Motivates explicit scope, transparent limitations and tests that examine security and usability together.
Compare HMEG against reproducible single-detector baselines and test source-held-out data rather than assuming benchmark transfer.
Motivates intent-sensitive detection and end-to-end evaluation; a prompt classifier alone cannot prove downstream model safety.
Evaluate the robustness of HMEG fusion against held-out attack mechanisms; distinguish this from a claim to reproduce EGUARD.
Direct methodological support for a frozen embedding model followed by a classifier. HMEG treats this as one expert, not the entire decision system.
Evaluate calibration and efficiency explicitly while keeping HMEG independent of target-LLM logits.
Compare HMEG against flat fusion under a genuinely held-out protocol, and select thresholds only on validation data.
Feature engineering and complementary rule/model signals can inform English-only experiments. No multilingual capability is claimed for HMEG.
Motivates clear augmentation provenance and explainability checks. HMEG must separately test false positives on unseen English data.
Provides an LLM-based comparison and motivates separating harmful-content classification from jailbreak-specific evaluation.
Use complementary expert responsibilities while measuring whether extra stages justify their latency.
Motivates testing staged computation and complementary evidence. HMEG uses learned expert classifiers; it does not reproduce this multi-agent framework.
Combine structural evidence with other HMEG experts and audit short-prompt false positives separately.
Motivates separate English OOD evaluation, frozen threshold selection and false-positive analysis. Similar signals do not prove HMEG’s router is effective.
Test whether heterogeneous expert fusion improves HMEG robustness without the runtime cost of a multi-LLM guardrail.
Measure HMEG robustness to character obfuscation without equating unusual formatting with malicious intent.
Measure HMEG false positives, routing cost and generalization within one controlled protocol.
Keep HMEG jailbreak labels distinct from harmful-topic and refusal labels, and audit coverage of benign prompts.
